task.description:
Design a fix for GH #504 / ISS-0176 (LUA-07 criterion 2). ISSUE-FIXER's investigation (Step 1, handoff 8f052f0f) found something significant: there is currently NO engine call site invoking the Lua executor at all -- grep -rn 'ScriptResult|executeScript' src/engine/ returns zero matches, and src/design/lua-integration.md's full 3-phase Implementation Roadmap (section 25) never lists actual SERVICE_TASK-with-script engine invocation as in-scope for any phase. ScriptResult/executeScriptWithManifest are currently only ever called from src/lua/'s own test files. This means the issue's literal acceptance criteria (an integration test where 'executing a script' produces an audit row) cannot be satisfied via a small plumbing fix to an EXISTING call site, because no such call site exists.

USER-CONFIRMED SCOPE DECISION (via ORCH, explicit business decision, not an autonomous inference): build MINIMAL, NARROW synthetic engine-side wiring -- a real, genuine call path in src/engine/ that invokes the Lua executor (executeScriptWithManifest or equivalent) and writes manifest_hash to an audit row -- WITHOUT building the full SERVICE_TASK integration described across all 3 roadmap phases. This is deliberately narrower than a complete feature: it should be the smallest real (not fake/mocked) code path that satisfies LUA-07's literal acceptance criteria (engine consumes ScriptResult, persists manifest_hash to a queryable audit record, integration test proves it end-to-end, mutation-checked). Design this scope precisely: what is the minimal, real trigger point in the engine for 'a script executes' that doesn't require building the full SERVICE_TASK node-type handling described in lua-integration.md's roadmap? Consider: is there an existing engine extension point (a hook, a pluggable executor interface) that a narrow Lua-invocation path could attach to without a large surrounding feature? Or does a defensible minimal scope mean creating a small, explicitly-labeled 'synthetic execution entry point' used ONLY by this fix's integration test, clearly documented as a stand-in for the eventual full SERVICE_TASK wiring, not presented as if it were that wiring? Also design the audit-record schema change (ISSUE-FIXER found neither audit_entries nor audit_log has a manifest_hash column -- decide new column vs new table vs reuse of audit_log.detail JSONB, with rationale) -- this needs a migration.
acceptance_criteria: A precise, minimal scope defined for the engine-side call path -- explicitly narrower than the full SERVICE_TASK roadmap feature, and honestly labeled as such (not disguised as complete engine integration)
Audit-record schema decision made with rationale (new column / new table / reuse existing JSONB) and a migration designed if needed
Design confirms the resulting integration test genuinely exercises real code (not a mock), satisfying LUA-07s literal acceptance criteria
Design explicitly notes what remains out of scope (full SERVICE_TASK engine integration) so this is not mistaken for that larger feature being complete
No implementation code present in the design artefact

result.summary: Designed minimal, honest engine-side wiring for LUA-07 criterion 2: new src/engine/lua_script_audit.zig::executeScriptForAudit calls the existing lua_executor.executeScriptWithManifest and persists ScriptResult.manifest_hash into a new purpose-built table lua_script_execution_audit (manifest_hash BYTEA NOT NULL, indexed). Rejected reusing audit_entries (trigger-fed only, never fires for script execution) and audit_log.detail (weakens the mutation test). Rejected attaching to the EXT-03 plugin_registry SERVICE_TASK dispatch point because no production bootstrap registers any handler there today -- doing so would silently build real SERVICE_TASK script dispatch, which is explicitly out of scope. The only caller of executeScriptForAudit after this fix is the new integration test (tests/integration/iss0176_lua07_audit_manifest_hash_test.zig); this is stated plainly in the function doc comment and in design sections 0, 2.3 and 6 so it cannot be mistaken for full SERVICE_TASK integration. Design confirms the mutation-check property: deleting the INSERT or the manifest_hash column binding makes the integration test fail (section 5).
